title: The processes of a launcher's running stage end when the launcher ends
outcome: The processes of a launcher's running stage end when the launcher ends
acceptance: On Windows, when the launcher process is killed during a stage, every process that stage started ends without any cleanup by the test: a regression starts the real chain of the Rust stage (wrapper, cargo, a parked test binary with a child), kills only the launcher, and finds none of them alive, holding each by its process id and creation time

The containment is one kill-on-close job that the launcher process itself owns, set up once before the first stage; each stage process is created suspended by a small helper, assigned to that job and then resumed, so that everything the stage starts is inside the job from its first instruction; the helper holds no handle to the job while the stage runs; no command-line search, parent-id walk or process-tree kill takes its place
The host's credit is unchanged: a foreground full or focused run is started by the same command as before, and its record lines keep their grammar

When the job cannot be set up, the run continues, its result records containment as unavailable with the reason, and the summary prints it; it is never silent; and each stage's command line, working directory, environment, log bytes and exit code are the same as without the helper
